messages:
maya: quick note from tonight's nova-lite-int8 canary: streaming funcall outputs show chunk-boundary JSON fragmentation causing parser failures. fp16 baseline streaming fine (0.6%); nova-int8 streaming = 2.9% parse fail in production canary.
maya: symptoms: valid JSON object split across websocket/chunk frames; parser sees partial object and errors instead of waiting for stream end
kevin: can you paste a raw stream capture?
maya: sure. raw capture (chunks shown with >>):
```
>> {\"action\": \"create_event\", \"data\": {\"title\": \"Deploy day\",
>> \"time\": \"2026-03-21T15:00:00Z\"}}
```
kevin: looks fine?
maya: that's the reassembled view. raw frames we see:
```
frame1: {\"action\": \"create_event\", \"data\": {\"title\": \"Deploy day\",\nframe2: \"time\": \"2026-03-21T15:00:00Z\"}}
```
maya: our parser attempts to parse per-frame (we have streaming parse enabled to surface funcalls early) and errors on frame1: "unexpected end of JSON input"
luis: aha. so it's a client-side streaming-parse policy + model chunking interaction. why only int8?
kevin: hypothesis: int8 attention kernels push slightly different tokenization boundaries; streaming flush policy emits smaller chunks for some samples -> increases probability of split across JSON tokens/newlines
sre-bot: alert: nova-lite-int8 canary parse_fail_rate=2.9% (+2.3% delta vs baseline)
maya: repro: replaying the same prompt with streaming disabled yields 0% parse fails; enabling streaming parse on fp16 also reproduces errors but at a much lower rate.
luis: mitigation ideas: 1) don't parse per-frame; buffer until full JSON sentinel ("}" matched) or streaming-trailer marker, 2) ask runtime to prefer larger chunk flush (change flush_threshold), 3) envelope payload into single-line NDJSON so each line is self-contained, 4) increase funcall retry budget and add robust repair heuristics that join last two frames and retry parse.
kevin: NDJSON seems the least invasive for now: server emits one-line JSON per funcall call. downside: longer lines, but parser becomes line-oriented and resilient to frame splits.
maya: prototype NDJSON shim done in postprocess: we replace newlines inside payload with \u2424 and emit single-line json. early tests: parse_fail rate drops to 0.7% for int8 streaming.
luis: good. but we should also fix root cause: downstream kernel flush behavior. file a kernel/regression ticket for int8 chunk-size distribution. attach tokenization histogram for int8 vs fp16.
kevin: also add a conservative client fallback: if streaming parser fails on a frame, buffer next frame and retry join prior+current before marking fail. cheap and immediate.
maya: agreed. i'll push the NDJSON shim to canary (canary flag: use_stream_ndjson=true) and add streaming-join retry logic to client libs.
sre-bot: Canary update scheduled: 5k samples with use_stream_ndjson=true starting 1743570000 UTC.
deploy-bot: Canary run kicked off by maya.
kevin: action items: (1) maya: push shim + client-join retry, (2) luis: open kernel ticket with flush histograms + int8 kernel owner cc, (3) ops: monitor parse_fail metric by chunk_size and model variant.
maya: will attach three raw failing trace captures to the ticket. thanks :thumbsup:
